newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Italian serie A game due to be played on Sunday (league positions in brackets, kick-off times GMT):

With German striker Oliver Bierhoff back in full-time action after nearly three months, visitors Udinese represent serious opposition for a Bologna side whose recent good run was halted by a 2-0 defeat by AC Milan last Sunday. Brazilian Amoroso partners Bierhoff in the Udinese attack while Bologna rely on Swede Kennet Andersson and Russian Igor Kolyvanov up front.
Relegation battle par excellence in which Cagliari look to Sandro Tovalieri and Roberto Muzzi to strike against a Verona side boosted by an unexpected 2-1 home win against Fiorentina last week.

Argentine Gabriel Batistuta will be partnered by Russian Andreij Kanchelskis in a vital game for the home team, while leaders Juventus look to Michele Padovano and Alessandro Del Piero in attack. Juventus have won the last two league encounters 1-0, in March and September 1996.

Another difficult home test for Inter against the most in-form side in the league who are unbeaten since November 24. Inter coach Roy Hodgson may opt for an attacking formation with Chilean Ivan Zamorano partnered by Maurizio Ganz. Dutchman Aron Winter replaces suspended Swiss midfielder Ciriaco Sforza, while Englishman Paul Ince may be ruled out by injury. Atalanta field a full-strength formation led by Domenico Morfeo, winger Gigi Lentini and Filippo Inzaghi, the league's leading goalscorer on 15.

Captain Roberto Mancini returns from suspension for this difficult away tie against a Napoli side surprisingly beaten 1-0 by Piacenza last Sunday. Vincenzo Montella partners Mancini in attack, while injured defender Moreno Mannini is replaced by Frenchman Oumar Dieng. Napoli hope that Brazilian Beto can compensate for the injury enforced absence of his compatriot Andre Cruz.

Both Parma and Lazio will want to improve on draws last Sunday, against Reggiana and Inter respectively. Lazio will be without Australian midfielder Paul Okon and Italian international striker Pierluigi Casiraghi, due to be replaced by Dario Marcolin and Igor Protti. Parma look to Argentine Hernan Crespo and Enrico Chiesa in attack, with Croat Mario Stanic in midfield.

Such is Milan's dependence on their Liberian striker George Weah that the club will send a private jet to Tanzania to bring Weah back to Italy early on Sunday after his African Nations Cup game for Liberia against Tanzania. Weah may be asked to play the second half against Perugia and Milan should prove too strong with Frenchman Christophe Dugarry and Marco Simone in attack. Perugia look to Brazilian Muller partnered by Croat Milan Rapajic.
A full-strength Roma led by Francesco Totti and Argentine Abel Balbo, on the 14 goal mark, should prove too strong for the bottom side in the league, led by Russian striker Igor Simutenkov.

One-time league leaders Vicenza have lost their way recently, losing to Milan, Roma and Atalanta in three of their last five games. Uruguyan Marcel Otero and Roberto Murgita lead the Vicenza attack against relegation battlers Piacenza, led by Pasquale Luiso and Giuseppe Scienza.
